title: Recover bounded reads through Path Session artifacts
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Add selector-driven bounded reads and lossless recovery: rfs_read supports ranges, raw projections, and lower-only limits, and successful omitted output spills to immutable artifact Resources owned by one Path Session with quotas, disconnect invalidation, and TTL cleanup.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Range, multi-range, raw, and paging selectors return exact requested content and name valid continuation selectors.
- [ ] Per-call limits may lower but never raise the hard text, line, and column ceilings.
- [ ] Omitted successful output is losslessly recoverable through an immutable artifact reference in the same Path Session.
- [ ] Object/session quota exhaustion fails with a bounded limit error without evicting a live reference or claiming lost content is recoverable.
- [ ] Disconnect invalidates session references and TTL cleanup removes retained backing state without crossing sessions.
- [ ] The Artifact Source Adapter is directly tested and the golden corpus covers selectors, limits, paging, spill, and recovery.

## Blocked by

- rfs-cgbq — Resolve safe multi-root Workspace References

notes.content: Closed: Implemented in commits through e44ad17: selector-driven bounded reads, immutable artifact recovery/continuations, durable per-connection Path Sessions, quota and TTL storage, strict lower-only MCP limits, cancellation/EOF late-commit fences, and observable storage failures. Verified by 96 workspace tests, the 21-row independent selector oracle, rmcp disconnect probe, strict Clippy, and final review with no P0-P2 findings.

title: Mutate workspace text with versioned writes and hashline edits
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Implement safe workspace text mutation through rfs_write and rfs_edit: create, replace, patch, delete, and same-source move use content-derived Version Tags, seen-region snapshots, separate grants, stale-state rejection, per-Resource serialization, and atomic replacement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] rfs_write creates UTF-8 text only when create is granted and replaces existing text only with its current ifVersion tag and update grant.
- [ ] Hashline PUT and CUT operate only against the exact Version Tag and displayed regions captured by a prior read.
- [ ] REM is the only deletion form; same-source MV requires delete/create grants and cross-source moves are rejected.
- [ ] Stale, guessed-unseen, malformed, and conflicting patches leave authoritative content unchanged and return stable errors.
- [ ] Concurrent mutations serialize per canonical Resource and filesystem commits are atomic on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- [ ] Filesystem mutation contracts are directly tested and hashline parsing is fuzzed.

## Blocked by

- rfs-34pz — Recover bounded reads through Path Session artifacts
- rfs-r9m6 — Operate ResourceFS from one strict Server Profile

notes.content: rfs-ewh2 spec decision (approved 2026-08-22): rfs:// and rfs://workspace are unconditionally immutable catalog Resources. When rfs_write/rfs_edit land, mutation attempts against either reference must return permission_denied and leave state unchanged. rfs-ewh2 classifies immutability now; this issue owns end-to-end tool enforcement.

title: Serve and read one workspace file over MCP
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Build the first complete ResourceFS path: an installable Rust binary starts as a stdio MCP server, negotiates supported protocol revisions, exposes rfs_read, resolves one explicitly launched Primary Workspace Root, and returns a small UTF-8 file as complete text plus object-root structured content through the real MCP interface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The compiled binary serves MCP over clean stdio and exposes rfs_read with an object-root input/output schema.
- [ ] The server advertises MCP 2026-07-28, negotiates 2025-11-25 where the SDK supports it, and gates optional capabilities.
- [ ] Reading a contained UTF-8 file under one explicit Primary Workspace Root returns exact text and equivalent structured fields.
- [ ] Missing, invalid, directory-as-file, and out-of-root inputs surface stable observable error categories.
- [ ] The filesystem Source Adapter has direct contract tests in addition to the compiled-process MCP test.

## Blocked by

- None — can start immediately.

notes.content: Closed: Implemented by commits 2ca713d, 8c13e09, and ffb699e: source-neutral read contracts, a contained bounded filesystem adapter, and the installable resourcefs stdio MCP binary. Final proof: rmcp probe/oracle PASS, cargo test --workspace 23/23 PASS, full clippy PASS, raw cargo-run MCP initialize/list/read/clean-exit PASS, and Cargo installation PASS.

Follow-on accepted bounded-read/Path-Session contract completed in e44ad17: strict lower-only rfs_read limits; complete source projections through one spill/recovery engine; durable per-connection heartbeat; request-cancel and EOF late-commit fences; observable write/disconnect storage failures. Final proof: 96 workspace tests across 16 suites, 21-row independent selector oracle, rmcp 3.1.3 disconnect probe, strict all-target/all-feature Clippy, and no P0-P2 final-review findings.

title: Resolve safe multi-root Workspace References
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Make Workspace Reference identity complete across client and launch roots: all tools resolve relative, contained absolute, file URI, and canonical rfs workspace inputs with deterministic Primary Workspace Root selection, private canonical identity, Windows parsing, literal-selector precedence, canonical containment, and root-change invalidation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Non-empty client MCP Roots override launch roots; otherwise exactly one of profile roots or CLI roots supplies authority.
- [ ] Relative references require a unique Primary Workspace Root, while canonical rfs workspace references address every declared root.
- [ ] Canonical Resource identity remains private rfs URI; backing file URI metadata appears only when explicitly enabled.
- [ ] Traversal, escaping symlinks or reparse points, ambiguous roots, and removed-root snapshots/references are rejected.
- [ ] Windows drive/UNC forms and literal-selector precedence behave deterministically on the platform matrix.
- [ ] A golden reference corpus and reference-parser fuzz harness cover accepted and rejected forms.

## Blocked by

- rfs-87cv — Serve and read one workspace file over MCP

notes.content: Implemented safe multi-root Workspace References end to end: strict path grammar and private canonical IDs; capability-contained launch/client root resolution; unique primary selection; literal-before-selector reads; atomic client Roots replacement/fallback; per-generation stale-result rejection; serialized request-associated five-second acquisition with rmcp cancellation; strict client display names; native-platform absolute mapping; and hidden-by-default backing paths. Review decisions F1–F10 are recorded in .rfs-cgbq/review-decisions.md. Final proof: 51 tests across 9 all-feature suites; strict Clippy; Rust 1.88; Windows MSVC and macOS target checks; rmcp and independent oracles; Wine/Win32 probe; release install plus CLI smoke; exactly 10,000 parser fuzz runs. Full checkpoint evidence is in .rfs-cgbq/plan.md.
Closed: Implemented and verified the accepted safe multi-root Workspace Reference contract.

title: Describe the namespace from its rfs:// root
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Implement ADR-0005's discovery commitment (docs/adr/0005-consolidating-namespace.md): rfs_read of rfs:// returns a bounded, read-only catalog of the mounted address space — every active source scheme, its one-line reference grammar, and one valid example spelling — and rfs://workspace enumerates declared Workspace Roots. Entries derive from the compiled Source Adapter registry so each future source appears in the catalog without catalog-specific work. This is the entry point that lets an unconfigured harness discover the address space through the tools alone, and it should land before the Kiro acceptance scenario (rfs-5os7) exercises a real agent against the server.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] rfs_read of rfs:// returns a bounded catalog naming every mounted source scheme with a one-line reference grammar and one valid example spelling.
- [ ] Catalog entries derive from the compiled Source Adapter registry; configured-but-degraded sources are visibly marked and no unmounted scheme is advertised as resolvable.
- [ ] rfs_read of rfs://workspace enumerates declared Workspace Roots and marks the Primary Workspace Root; the listing tracks client root-set changes.
- [ ] Catalog resources are read-only: every mutation attempt fails explicitly regardless of workspace or source grants.
- [ ] Catalog output uses the common limits, result, and error contracts, including complete non-empty text plus structured content.
- [ ] Tool descriptions and server initialization instructions name rfs:// as the discovery entry point.
- [ ] Direct tests cover catalog content against mounted sources, degraded-source marking, workspace-root enumeration after a root-set change, and mutation rejection.

notes.content: Prioritized per ADR-0005: the discovery entry point for the namespace; should land before the Kiro acceptance scenario (rfs-5os7).

title: Read allowlisted HTTPS Resources safely
description:
## Parent

This slice also proves required and Degraded Source lifecycle and connectivity probes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Allowlisted HTTPS reads return deterministic reader-mode content; raw selectors return the bounded original body.
- [ ] Search, limits, cancellation, MIME/encoding handling, and Recovery References use the common contracts.
- [ ] Every redirect and resolved address is reauthorized; private/special addresses require a distinct grant.
- [ ] Host, credential, and source policy denial surfaces stable errors without leaking secrets.
- [ ] Unavailable required sources fail startup; optional sources become visibly Degraded and fail only their references.
- [ ] An explicit non-mutating probe reports connectivity; controlled HTTP fixtures directly test the Source Adapter.

## Blocked by

- rfs-vl0u — Search and glob workspace Resources
- rfs-r9m6 — Operate ResourceFS from one strict Server Profile

notes.content: Prioritized per ADR-0005: read-only consolidation win — retires an MCP server from agent configuration. Unblocked once the Server Profile (rfs-r9m6) lands.

Substrate charter: build this as the project's one bounded HTTP substrate, then HTTPS reader mode on top of it. The substrate (owned by resourcefs-sources, source-neutral types in core) must provide: profile host allowlist enforcement, per-redirect and per-resolved-address revalidation, private/loopback/link-local address policy behind the separate per-host grant, bounded response bodies and timeouts, TLS via one chosen client crate, and a deterministic fake-server test helper. Consumers: rfs-45ww/rfs-by2z (GitHub over native HTTP APIs) and rfs-azd3 (Streamable HTTP downstream MCP) reuse it rather than adding a second client or policy layer. No HTTP client dependency exists in the workspace today; this issue introduces the only one.

title: Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server
description:
## Problem Statement

Users who value Oh My Pi’s path-shaped resource workflow cannot use that model from other agent harnesses. Files, archive members, database rows, remote objects, generated output, and session artifacts currently require different tool schemas, different routing knowledge, and often large inline payloads. Foreign harnesses do not inherit OMP’s internal URI router, session registries, prompts, permission model, or artifact lifecycle, so copying the existing tools would either fail or couple another product to OMP internals.

From the user’s perspective, the missing product is a portable Path Resource Server: one small, consistent interface that lets an agent name information first, materialize only the needed projection, preserve omitted content through Recovery References, and mutate authoritative text safely. It must remain useful in clients with incomplete MCP support, must not expose more filesystem or network authority than the operator granted, and must remain inspectable when results outlive one model turn.

ResourceFS currently has an accepted domain model, Behavior Contract, and architecture decisions but no implementation. The implementation must turn that accepted design into a standalone, distributable Rust product without becoming an OMP compatibility wrapper.

## Solution

Build ResourceFS 1.0 as an independent Rust workspace and `resourcefs` binary serving local stdio MCP. The canonical model-controlled interface consists of five deep tools: `rfs_read`, `rfs_search`, `rfs_glob`, `rfs_write`, and `rfs_edit`. These tools share one Path Reference grammar across Workspace Roots, session resources, archives, SQLite, HTTPS, GitHub, SSH, skills, rules, memory, vaults, imported agent history, and downstream MCP Resources.

ResourceFS will bound every result, preserve recoverable omitted content as immutable `artifact://` Resources, and return complete non-empty text alongside structured objects. It will mirror the same address space through MCP Resources and templates when negotiated, while keeping tools authoritative for model-controlled use. One MCP connection owns one Path Session containing Session Scratch, artifacts, snapshots, caches, and mutation journals.

Mutation will be text-only, explicitly granted per Workspace Root or Portable Source, protected by content-derived Version Tags, and serialized per canonical Resource. Source Adapters will hide source-specific resolution, projection, versioning, mutation, enumeration, and policy behavior behind a shared engine. ResourceFS will support Kiro CLI as the required 1.0 acceptance harness while remaining standard MCP for other clients.

## User Stories

1. As an agent-harness user, I want one resource interface across local and external information, so that my agent does not need a different tool model for every source.
2. As a Kiro CLI user, I want to launch ResourceFS as a local MCP server, so that I can use path-shaped resource operations without installing OMP.
3. As a coding agent, I want Resources to have stable Path References, so that I can pass references between tools instead of copying content.
4. As a coding agent, I want to request only the projection I need, so that irrelevant content does not consume my context window.
5. As a coding agent, I want omitted output to remain recoverable, so that bounded responses do not destroy information.
6. As an operator, I want ResourceFS to be independent of OMP configuration and runtime state, so that it can run under any MCP-capable harness.
7. As a maintainer, I want ResourceFS to own its Behavior Contract, so that product evolution is explicit rather than accidental OMP coupling.
8. As a caller, I want the product version to identify Behavior Contract compatibility, so that breaking changes require a major SemVer release.
9. As a user, I want Linux, macOS, and Windows releases, so that the same workflow works across my development machines.
10. As a Rust user, I want to install ResourceFS through Cargo, so that I have a source-based distribution path in addition to prebuilt binaries.
11. As a coding agent, I want relative filesystem references to resolve only under the Primary Workspace Root, so that their meaning is deterministic.
12. As a coding agent, I want to address non-primary roots with canonical `rfs://workspace/<root>/<path>` references, so that multi-root resources remain unambiguous.
13. As an operator, I want canonical workspace Resource identities to avoid absolute backing paths, so that normal tool output does not leak local directory structure.
14. As an operator, I want backing `file://` metadata to require explicit profile opt-in, so that path disclosure is a deliberate choice.
15. As a Windows user, I want drive and UNC paths parsed as filesystem references rather than URI schemes, so that ordinary paths work correctly.
16. As a coding agent, I want existing literal paths to win over selector parsing, so that names containing colon-like syntax remain addressable.
17. As a coding agent, I want ambiguous literal `:`, `?`, and `#` characters to have one percent-encoding rule, so that references round-trip losslessly.
18. As a coding agent, I want selectors to append consistently to filesystem and internal references, so that range and projection recovery uses one grammar.
19. As a coding agent, I want Path References to remain server-relative, so that I know to return them to the issuing ResourceFS process.
20. As an operator, I want built-in scheme registration conflicts to fail startup, so that reference meaning never depends on registration order.
21. As a caller, I want invalid Path References to fail with a stable error category, so that I can distinguish syntax failures from missing Resources.
22. As a caller, I want ambiguous downstream references to fail explicitly, so that configuration order never silently chooses a source.
23. As a coding agent, I want `rfs_read` to accept one `path` interface across every source, so that reading remains a deep module rather than many shallow tools.
24. As a coding agent, I want per-call read limits to lower profile caps, so that I can request smaller responses without inventing another selector grammar.
25. As a coding agent, I want parseable code reads to return Structural Summaries by default, so that declarations are visible without loading bodies.
26. As a Rust developer, I want Rust declarations summarized structurally, so that large Rust modules remain navigable.
27. As a TypeScript or JavaScript developer, I want declarations summarized structurally, so that module interfaces remain visible without implementation bodies.
28. As a Python developer, I want declarations summarized structurally, so that classes and functions remain navigable.
29. As a Go developer, I want declarations summarized structurally, so that package interfaces remain navigable.
30. As a Java developer, I want declarations summarized structurally, so that types and methods remain navigable.
31. As a C or C++ developer, I want declarations summarized structurally, so that native code remains navigable.
32. As a C# developer, I want declarations summarized structurally, so that .NET code remains navigable.
33. As a developer using another language, I want bounded text fallback, so that unsupported parsers do not make files unreadable.
34. As a coding agent, I want every Structural Summary to name exact recovery selectors, so that I never guess omitted ranges.
35. As a coding agent, I want directories to render as bounded listings, so that structure discovery does not flood the result.
36. As a coding agent, I want archive members to read through the same interface as files, so that I do not need to extract archives manually.
37. As a coding agent, I want SQLite rows to read as versioned JSON Resources, so that database content is inspectable and editable at resource granularity.
38. As a coding agent, I want HTTPS documents cleaned into reader-mode Markdown by default, so that page chrome does not consume context.
39. As a coding agent, I want a `:raw` HTTPS projection, so that I can recover the bounded original response when exact bytes matter.
40. As a coding agent, I want converted document formats to return text projections, so that non-plain-text documents remain searchable.
41. As a multimodal agent, I want image reads to include typed image content and complete text metadata, so that both image-aware and text-only paths remain useful.
42. As a text-only agent, I want unsupported binary Resources to return bounded metadata rather than garbage text, so that I understand why content was not embedded.
43. As a notebook user, I want notebooks rendered as deterministic cell-oriented text, so that cells can be read and edited without manipulating raw JSON.
44. As a notebook user, I want retained cell metadata and outputs preserved through edits, so that changing source does not discard unrelated notebook state.
45. As a coding agent, I want `rfs_search` to search referenced content without embedding it first, so that search remains lazy and context-efficient.
46. As a coding agent, I want Rust regex by default and PCRE2 for unsupported syntax, so that common searches stay fast while advanced patterns remain possible.
47. As a coding agent, I want search output grouped and paginated with Recovery References, so that large match sets remain navigable.
48. As a coding agent, I want `rfs_glob` to enumerate structures across capable sources, so that discovery uses one bounded interface.
49. As a coding agent, I want globbing to respect hidden and ignore controls, so that searches match repository conventions.
50. As an operator, I want network-backed completion excluded from keystroke-time discovery, so that autocomplete remains fast and predictable.
51. As a coding agent, I want `rfs_write` to create UTF-8 text Resources, so that new files, notes, scratch documents, and source-native text objects share one interface.
52. As a coding agent, I want existing-resource replacement to require `ifVersion`, so that a stale full write cannot silently overwrite newer content.
53. As a coding agent, I want `rfs_edit` to apply line-anchored hashline patches, so that edits target the exact Resource state I read.
54. As a coding agent, I want Version Tags to derive from authoritative content rather than timestamps, so that concurrency checks are content-accurate.
55. As a coding agent, I want edit snapshots to record which regions were displayed, so that guessed unseen line edits are rejected.
56. As a coding agent, I want `REM` to be the only deletion form, so that deletion is explicit in the patch language.
57. As a coding agent, I want same-source `MV` to be the only move form, so that move semantics remain source-native and reviewable.
58. As an operator, I want cross-source moves rejected, so that a nominal move cannot hide a copy-plus-delete across different authorities.
59. As an operator, I want moves to require delete authority at the source and create authority at the destination, so that permissions compose correctly.
60. As an operator, I want create, update, and delete grants configured separately, so that writable does not become an all-or-nothing flag.
61. As an operator, I want Source Mutation grants distinct from Workspace Mutation grants, so that remote authority is explicit.
62. As a caller, I want failed mutation validation to leave the Resource unchanged, so that errors are atomic from my perspective.
63. As a caller, I want concurrent mutations serialized per canonical Resource, so that in-process races do not corrupt state.
64. As a caller, I want source-native transactions or atomic replacement where available, so that partial writes are not observable.
65. As an operator, I want arbitrary binary writes rejected, so that the text/version contract remains coherent.
66. As an archive user, I want member create, replace, edit, delete, and same-archive move, so that archives act as contained mutable sources when granted.
67. As a security-conscious archive user, I want absolute and traversing member names rejected, so that archive operations cannot escape containment.
68. As a SQLite user, I want scalar and composite primary keys represented canonically, so that every safely addressable row has a stable identity.
69. As a SQLite user, I want path keys and JSON row keys validated for agreement, so that writes cannot target one row while describing another.
70. As a SQLite user, I want row mutations transactional, so that constraints and failures never leave partial state.
71. As an operator, I want arbitrary mutating SQL excluded, so that SQLite authority remains resource-level rather than database-wide command execution.
72. As a GitHub user, I want issue and PR aggregates readable, so that an agent can inspect remote work items through Path References.
73. As a GitHub user, I want authoritative title, body, and conversation comments exposed as separate Field Resources, so that edits do not overwrite rendered aggregates.
74. As a GitHub user, I want `comments/new` to create conversation comments and return their canonical references, so that comment creation composes with subsequent reads.
75. As a GitHub user, I want issue creation from strict title frontmatter plus Markdown, so that a text-only write can create a complete issue.
76. As a GitHub user, I want PR creation from title, head, base, optional draft, and Markdown body, so that the required PR identity is explicit.
77. As a GitHub user, I want remote Creation Targets to require `operationId`, so that safe repeats within one Path Session return the original result.
78. As a GitHub user, I want operation-ID reuse with different content rejected, so that one logical operation cannot change meaning.
79. As a GitHub user, I want unknown upstream creation outcomes reported without automatic retry, so that ResourceFS does not create duplicates.
80. As a GitHub user, I want conversation comments distinct from reviews and inline review comments, so that PR comment semantics remain stable.
81. As an operator, I want GitHub readable repositories allowlisted, so that a credential cannot expose every repository it can see.
82. As an operator, I want GitHub mutation grants narrower than read authority, so that inspection does not imply modification.
83. As an SSH user, I want contained read-only `ssh://` Resources using system SSH, so that existing host configuration and host-key checks remain authoritative.
84. As an operator, I want SSH host aliases allowlisted, so that a model cannot connect to arbitrary hosts.
85. As an Agent Skills user, I want `skill://` to resolve standard `SKILL.md` content and contained files, so that instructions are first-class Resources.
86. As a rule author, I want native rules defined by a versioned manifest plus Markdown, so that names, descriptions, glob scope, and content evolve explicitly.
87. As a project-memory user, I want `memory://` to expose configured memory read-only, so that recall does not imply mutation.
88. As an Obsidian user, I want `vault://` to understand note paths, wikilinks, properties, tasks, and bases, so that vault content remains semantically navigable.
89. As an Obsidian user, I want grant-controlled note mutations to preserve unrelated frontmatter, so that targeted edits do not damage note metadata.
90. As a harness integrator, I want `agent://` and `history://` backed by a public versioned Agent Export manifest, so that imports do not depend on private harness layouts.
91. As a harness integrator, I want imported agent outputs and transcripts read-only, so that ResourceFS cannot rewrite another harness’s history.
92. As an MCP user, I want downstream Resources and templates readable through `mcp://`, so that ResourceFS can unify external MCP resource catalogs.
93. As an MCP operator, I want downstream MCP stdio commands expressed as argv arrays, so that no shell interpretation occurs.
94. As an MCP operator, I want downstream Streamable HTTP restricted to allowlisted HTTPS hosts, so that proxying does not become arbitrary network access.
95. As an MCP operator, I want downstream native Resource URIs globally unique, so that a reference never changes meaning with source order.
96. As a caller, I want `/home/dwalleck/.omp/agent/sessions/-repos-oh-my-pi/2026-08-18T02-52-52-195Z_01a012c9-3863-7000-a568-fa76cdae77fc/local` Session Scratch writable without Workspace Mutation grants, so that agents always have a safe handoff and drafting space.
97. As a caller, I want Session Scratch writes subject to hard object/session quotas, so that always-writable authority does not imply unbounded storage.
98. As a caller, I want `artifact://` Recovery References immutable, so that omitted output cannot change after I receive its reference.
99. As a caller, I want live-session artifacts never evicted, so that returned Recovery References remain valid until disconnect.
100. As an operator, I want a failed lossless spill to return a bounded limit error, so that the server never pretends discarded output is recoverable.
101. As an operator, I want one MCP connection to own one Path Session, so that artifacts, scratch, snapshots, caches, and journals cannot collide across clients.
102. As an operator, I want Path Session references invalidated at disconnect, so that server-relative identities have a clear lifetime.
103. As an operator, I want expired session files garbage-collected after a TTL, so that recovery storage does not grow forever.
104. As an operator, I want MCP client roots to take precedence when supplied, so that the client’s declared filesystem authority is respected.
105. As an operator, I want either profile roots or CLI roots when client roots are absent, so that launch authority cannot silently union multiple sources.
106. As an operator, I want relative paths disabled until a Primary Workspace Root is unique, so that multi-root ambiguity cannot select the wrong workspace.
107. As an operator, I want root-set changes to invalidate snapshots and references tied to removed roots, so that stale authority is not retained.
108. As an operator, I want at most one strict versioned Server Profile, so that source and permission precedence remains visible.
109. As an operator, I want unknown profile fields and conflicting schemes rejected, so that misspelled security settings cannot be ignored.
110. As an operator, I want secrets referenced through environment variables or helper commands rather than embedded, so that profiles remain shareable.
111. As an operator, I want helpers, converters, and child servers to receive a minimal explicit environment, so that unrelated credentials are not inherited.
112. As an operator, I want subprocesses invoked directly without a shell, so that profile values cannot become shell programs.
113. As an operator, I want HTTPS redirects and resolved addresses revalidated, so that allowlisted origins cannot redirect into forbidden networks.
114. As an intranet user, I want private-network access to require a separate per-host grant, so that public-host authority does not imply internal-network authority.
115. As an operator, I want unavailable required sources to fail startup and optional sources to become visibly degraded, so that local tools remain usable without hiding required failures.
116. As a Kiro CLI user, I want every tool result to contain complete non-empty text, so that ignored structured content does not erase the result.
117. As a Kiro CLI user, I want every output schema rooted at an object, so that one schema cannot make Kiro reject the entire tool list.
118. As a Kiro CLI user, I want Recovery References rendered inline as text, so that unreliable `resource_link` support does not hide recovery paths.
119. As an MCP application, I want every resolvable Path Reference mirrored as a bounded Resource or template, so that UI-driven resource browsing uses the same address space.
120. As a release maintainer, I want real Kiro CLI acceptance in protected CI with a recorded interactive fallback, so that portability is proven against the required harness.

## Implementation Decisions

### Product and interface

- ResourceFS is an independent Rust product, repository, package, and release. OMP is design input, not a runtime dependency or continuing compatibility authority.
- The official Rust `rmcp` SDK provides the local stdio MCP runtime. ResourceFS advertises MCP `2026-07-28`, negotiates supported revisions, and feature-gates optional capabilities.
- Product SemVer is the Behavior Contract version. Breaking reference grammar, tool schema, result, or mutation semantics require a major release. Profile and import formats use separate integer schema versions.
- The canonical model-controlled interface is exactly five `rfs_*` tools: read, search, glob, write, and edit.
- All tools remain discoverable. Read-only/destructive annotations are advisory; the policy engine authorizes each operation against its resolved destination.
- `rfs_read`, `rfs_search`, and `rfs_glob` accept lower-only per-call limits. Selectors choose content projections; limit fields only constrain output.
- `rfs_write` accepts path, UTF-8 content, conditional Version Tag, and operation ID metadata. Replacements require the current Version Tag. Remote Creation Targets require an operation ID.
- `rfs_edit` accepts the versioned hashline patch language with line-anchored `PUT`, `CUT`, `REM`, and same-source `MV`.
- Every tool returns complete non-empty TextContent and a structured object. Every output schema has an object root.
- Tool errors expose stable semantic categories. MCP protocol/schema errors remain protocol errors.
- MCP Resources and templates mirror the same address space when negotiated. Tools remain canonical because client Resource support is inconsistent.
- Resource listing is bounded and paginated. Completion is local/fast. Only workspace/local and Path Session Resources publish subscription changes initially.
- No MCP Prompts or Tasks are exposed in 1.0. Essential instructions live early in tool descriptions and in initialization instructions.

### Reference and Resource contract

- A Path Reference contains a source namespace, Resource identity/hierarchy, and optional projection selector. The operation is never encoded as a new tool family.
- Existing literal filesystem paths take precedence over selector interpretation. Windows drives and UNC paths remain filesystem paths.
- Literal ambiguous delimiters are percent-encoded. Rendered references use canonical slash form.
- Relative paths resolve only under the Primary Workspace Root. Any declared root is directly addressable through canonical `rfs://workspace/<root>/<path>` input.
- Workspace MCP Resource identity remains private `rfs://` by default. Optional backing-path visibility adds `file://` metadata without changing canonical identity.
- Internal schemes are server-relative. ResourceFS preserves OMP-compatible spellings where portable but makes no global URI ownership claim.
- Included families are workspace files/directories, ZIP/tar archives, SQLite, HTTPS, converted documents, images, notebooks, session artifacts/scratch, memory, skills, rules, vaults, GitHub issues/PRs, SSH, Agent Exports, and downstream MCP Resources.
- OMP-runtime schemes for OMP docs, security findings, and tool devices are excluded.
- Downstream MCP proxies Resources/templates only, over direct-argv stdio or allowlisted Streamable HTTP. It never proxies tools or prompts.
- Known duplicate downstream native URIs fail configuration. Ambiguous template expansions fail at resolution.

### Projections and Source Adapters

- Parseable code defaults to Structural Summary. The compiled registry covers Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, C/C++, and C#. Unsupported or oversized inputs use bounded text fallback.
- Structural Summaries expose declarations, elide bodies, and name exact recovery selectors.
- Archive adapters enforce member containment and rebuild mutable archives through atomic replacement.
- SQLite rows are JSON Resources addressed by scalar or canonical composite keys. Writes insert or fully replace, edits operate on JSON projections, deletes use `REM`, and all mutations are transactional. Arbitrary mutating SQL is excluded.
- HTTPS defaults to reader-mode Markdown/text; `:raw` returns the bounded original body. Every redirect and resolved address is reauthorized.
- Document conversion is configured by direct argv and remains a read projection.
- Image reads return typed image content plus complete textual metadata. Unsupported arbitrary binary data is metadata/blob-readable but not mutable.
- Notebook reads use deterministic cell markers. Versioned edits preserve notebook metadata and retained cell metadata/outputs, support cell insertion/reorder/deletion, and reject malformed projections.
- GitHub aggregates are read-only. Title, body, and conversation comments are Field Resources.
- GitHub issue creation uses strict title frontmatter plus Markdown body. PR creation requires title/head/base, permits draft, and uses Markdown body.
- GitHub post-creation mutation is limited to title, body, and conversation comments. Labels, assignees, status, reviews, and inline review comments are read-only in 1.0.
- Operation IDs deduplicate only within one live Path Session. Reuse with different content fails. Unknown upstream outcomes are never automatically retried; callers reconcile before repeating after disconnect.
- SSH is read-only, uses system SSH/host-key verification, and permits only configured host aliases.
- Skills follow the Agent Skills format. Native rules use a strict versioned manifest mapping name, description, glob scope, and contained Markdown.
- Memory is a read-only configured file/directory projection.
- Vault Resources understand Obsidian notes, wikilinks, properties, tasks, and bases; grant-controlled text mutations preserve unrelated frontmatter.
- Agent/history imports use a public strict versioned manifest and contained files; they never inspect private harness layouts and remain read-only.
- `/home/dwalleck/.omp/agent/sessions/-repos-oh-my-pi/2026-08-18T02-52-52-195Z_01a012c9-3863-7000-a568-fa76cdae77fc/local` is caller-authored Session Scratch. `artifact://` is immutable server-authored recovery storage.

### Mutation, authority, and concurrency

- Workspace Roots and mutable Portable Sources declare independent create, update, and delete grants. Merely configuring an adapter grants no mutation.
- Version Tags derive from authoritative content rather than timestamps.
- Read snapshots bind Version Tags to the displayed projection/regions, preventing edits to guessed unseen content.
- Existing-resource writes require `ifVersion`; hashline edits carry the read header and Version Tag.
- Mutation validates current authoritative state immediately before commit and serializes per canonical Resource.
- Filesystem and archive mutation uses atomic replacement, SQLite uses transactions, and remote adapters use the strongest available compare-before-write behavior without claiming unavailable upstream atomicity.
- `REM` is the sole deletion syntax. `MV` is same-source only and requires delete/create authority. Cross-source moves and binary writes fail.
- Failed validation does not change authoritative state.

### Sessions, roots, configuration, and security

- One MCP connection owns one Path Session: artifacts, scratch, snapshots, caches, operation journal, and source handles.
- Disconnect invalidates Path Session references immediately. Cache files remain only until configured TTL cleanup.
- Non-empty client MCP Roots take precedence. Otherwise exactly one launch source supplies roots: one Server Profile or CLI roots, never both.
- Multiple roots require a uniquely matching primary-root selector before relative references work.
- Client root changes immediately re-derive authority, invalidate removed-root snapshots/references, and retain session-owned scratch/artifacts.
- At most one strict JSON Server Profile is loaded. Unknown fields, invalid policy, unsafe paths, and registration conflicts fail startup.
- Profiles configure sources, required/degraded behavior, mutation grants, repository/host/path allowlists, private-network grants, lower limits, session cache/TTL, backing-path visibility, secret references, converters, and downstream MCP definitions.
- Secrets are references, never inline values. Helper commands run without a shell, with hard time/output caps and only a minimal explicit environment.
- Required unavailable sources fail startup. Optional unavailable sources enter visible Degraded Source state and fail only their own references.
- HTTPS is host-allowlisted. Loopback, link-local, private, and special addresses require separate explicit grants and are revalidated across redirects/resolution.
- Canonical path containment follows real targets, including symlinks/reparse points. Archive paths receive equivalent containment checks.
- Logging never uses protocol stdout, redacts credentials, and emits no telemetry.
- The CLI exposes serve, check, and schema operations only. Configuration checking has an explicit non-mutating external probe mode.

### Limits, architecture, and distribution

- Built-in hard ceilings are 48 KiB/3,000 lines/512 columns for text results, 5 MiB per embedded image, 64 MiB per artifact or scratch object, 256 MiB per Path Session, and 1,000 entries per listing page.
- Profiles and calls may lower but never raise the binary’s hard ceilings.
- Omitted successful output spills losslessly to immutable Recovery References. A spill that would exceed quota fails with a bounded limit error. Live references are never evicted.
- The Rust workspace contains three principal deep modules: the core engine, compiled Source Adapters, and the MCP/CLI adapter.
- The core engine owns reference parsing, selectors, Resource/result/error types, policy, Path Sessions, snapshots/tags, limits, recovery, and mutation coordination.
- The sources module contains all compiled adapters. Configuration creates adapter instances; dynamic plugins are not supported.
- The MCP module owns protocol negotiation, schemas, content rendering, cancellation, Resources/templates/completion/subscriptions, Kiro compatibility, and CLI composition.
- A shared Source Adapter interface covers resolution, projection, versioning, enumeration, mutation, and source capability/policy behavior.
- GitHub uses native HTTP. SSH uses system SSH. Archives support ZIP/tar families. Structural parsing uses a curated tree-sitter registry. Search uses Rust regex plus PCRE2.
- Prebuilt Linux/macOS/Windows releases and `cargo install` are first-class distribution contracts.

## Testing Decisions

- The highest behavioral seam is the compiled `resourcefs` process over stdio MCP. End-to-end contract tests launch the real binary with temporary Workspace Roots and deterministic local/fake upstreams, then call the five tools and mirrored Resources exactly as a harness does.
- The user explicitly requires every Source Adapter to be tested directly in addition to the MCP seam. Direct adapter suites verify each source’s resolution, projection, versioning, enumeration, mutation, containment, and error mapping. Global behavior such as MCP rendering and Kiro fallbacks stays at the external seam rather than being duplicated in every adapter suite.
- A good test asserts externally observable behavior: returned text/structured content, canonical Path References, Version Tags, authoritative state changes, stable error categories, recovery, permissions, and boundedness. Tests do not assert private field assignment, helper call order, crate internals, or source text.
- The core engine receives focused contract and property tests for reference parsing, selector algebra, Version Tags, snapshot visibility, policy decisions, quota accounting, per-Resource mutation serialization, and Path Session/root transitions.
- Filesystem adapter tests cover relative/absolute/root-qualified references, multi-root primary selection, symlinks/reparse points, literal-selector precedence, Windows forms, atomic write failure, stale versions, `REM`, and same-source `MV`.
- Archive adapter tests cover ZIP/tar families, traversing/absolute member rejection, member reads/search/glob, create/replace/edit/delete/move, metadata preservation where promised, and atomic rebuild failure.
- SQLite adapter tests cover scalar/composite keys, canonical encoding, row JSON transformation, key mismatch, insert/replace/edit/delete, constraints, transactions, concurrency, invalid schema, and read-only queries.
- Document/image/notebook adapter tests cover converter failure/timeout/output caps, image metadata and payload ceilings, unsupported binary behavior, deterministic notebook projections, marker escaping, metadata/output preservation, type changes, insertion/reorder/deletion, invalid JSON, and malformed edits.
- HTTPS adapter tests use controlled servers to cover reader mode, raw mode, MIME/encoding, redirects, DNS/address revalidation, host/private-network policy, body limits, cancellation, and credential redaction.
- GitHub adapter tests use a deterministic fake HTTP upstream to cover repository allowlists, aggregate/Field Resource separation, title/body/comment mutation, issue/PR creation documents, conversation versus review comments, compare-before-write behavior, operation-ID reuse, unknown outcomes, and policy denial.
- SSH adapter tests use a controlled SSH fixture or argv-level executable fixture to cover host allowlists, normal host-key failure propagation, UTF-8/output caps, cancellation, minimal environment, and mutation rejection.
- Skill/rule/memory/vault tests cover manifest/schema validation, containment, symlink escape, Agent Skills resolution, rule glob metadata, read-only memory, vault wikilinks/properties/tasks/bases, frontmatter preservation, and grant-controlled mutations.
- Agent Export tests cover schema versions, parent/child relationships, stable IDs, contained paths, missing output/transcript files, malicious traversal, read-only behavior, and bounded listing.
- Downstream MCP adapter tests launch deterministic stdio and HTTP resource servers to cover negotiation, listing, templates, completion, native URI preservation, global collisions, ambiguous expansions, degraded/required sources, binary/text contents, limits, cancellation, and the absence of tool/prompt proxying.
- Session-resource adapter tests cover scratch create/replace/edit/delete/move, artifact immutability, object/session quotas, no live eviction, disconnect invalidation, TTL cleanup, operation journals, and cross-session isolation.
- Official MCP conformance suites verify supported negotiated server revisions. Output-schema regression fixtures require object roots and non-empty text fallbacks.
- The real Kiro CLI is a release acceptance seam. Protected CI runs startup, discovery, read, spill/recovery, search, scratch write/read, and permission denial with a secret; a recorded interactive run is the fallback where headless credentials are unavailable.
- Cross-platform binary smoke tests run on Linux, macOS, and Windows. They exercise path parsing, installation, process startup, stdio cleanliness, and one representative read/write/recovery scenario.
- Parser fuzzing targets Path Reference parsing, selector parsing, hashline patches, archive member names, percent encoding, composite SQLite keys, manifests, and strict profile schemas. Fuzzing supplements but does not replace behavioral assertions.
- Stress fixtures cover large files, deep directories, many search matches, maximum listings, large images, artifact/session exhaustion, concurrent operations, slow/cancelled sources, and parser fallback without unbounded memory growth.
- Prior art comes from OMP’s observable read-selector, internal-resource routing, hashline edit, notebook round-trip, output-spill, and MCP lifecycle behavior. ResourceFS copies useful fixture ideas into its own Behavior Contract rather than importing OMP implementation or asserting permanent parity.

## Out of Scope

- OMP runtime integration, OMP configuration discovery, private OMP session-layout inspection, or continuing OMP conformance.
- Remote or multi-tenant ResourceFS transport; 1.0 is a local stdio server.
- OMP-owned documentation, security-scan, or virtual tool-device schemes.
- Dynamic Source Adapter plugins.
- MCP Prompt or Task surfaces.
- Downstream MCP tool or prompt proxying.
- Arbitrary mutating SQL.
- Arbitrary binary mutation.
- Cross-source moves.
- SSH mutation.
- Mutable Memory Resources or imported agent/history data.
- GitHub labels, assignees, status, reviews, or inline-review mutation after object creation.
- Automatic retries after unknown remote creation outcomes.
- Cross-session operation-ID deduplication.
- Interactive profile management or a configuration UI.
- Telemetry.

## Further Notes

- The accepted domain glossary and ADRs are normative. Use the canonical terms Path Reference, Resource, Workspace Root, Portable Source, Path Session, Server Profile, Recovery Reference, Session Scratch, Workspace Mutation, Source Mutation, Mutation Policy, Structural Summary, Behavior Contract, Version Tag, Aggregate Resource, Field Resource, Creation Target, Agent Export, Resource Mirror, Degraded Source, Source Adapter, and Backing-Path Visibility.
- Kiro CLI is the compatibility floor, not the only intended client. Its current limitations require complete text fallbacks, object-root output schemas, inline Recovery References, and conservative output bounds.
- The official Rust MCP SDK was selected because it provides the required stdio server/client, tool, Resource/template, structured-content, cancellation, and conformance support. Experimental MCP Tasks are unnecessary.
- This issue specifies the complete 1.0 product. Subsequent ticket decomposition should preserve the accepted interfaces and split implementation by independently verifiable Behavior Contract slices rather than by crate scaffolding alone.

title: Summarize Rust code structurally
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Introduce the curated structural-parser registry through a complete Rust slice: Rust reads expose bounded declarations, elide bodies, name exact recovery selectors, and fall back safely for oversized or unparseable input.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rust functions, types, traits, impls, modules, constants, and relevant attributes appear in a stable Structural Summary while bodies are omitted.
- [ ] Every elided region names a selector that rfs_read can recover exactly.
- [ ] Unparseable, unsupported-encoding, and over-safety-limit inputs use bounded text fallback rather than partial invented structure.
- [ ] Summary output obeys the standard result limits and Recovery Reference contract.
- [ ] Parser-registry and Rust structural behavior are tested through rfs_read and focused parser fixtures.

## Blocked by

- rfs-34pz — Recover bounded reads through Path Session artifacts

notes.content: Deferred per ADR-0005 (consolidating namespace): retires no MCP server from an agent's configuration. Revisit after the consolidation sources (GitHub, memory, HTTPS, SQLite, vault) land.

title: Summarize Go, Java, and C# structurally
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Extend the structural-parser registry so Go, Java, and C# files receive language-correct bounded Structural Summaries and exact recovery selectors through the same read interface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Go declarations cover packages, imports, types, functions, methods, variables, and constants.
- [ ] Java and C# declarations cover namespaces/packages, types, members, generics, annotations/attributes, and nested types.
- [ ] Each elided body is recoverable through an exact selector and summaries remain bounded.
- [ ] Parse failure and oversized input use the common text fallback.
- [ ] Each language family has externally observable rfs_read fixtures plus focused parser tests.

title: Operate ResourceFS from one strict Server Profile
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Give operators one explicit, strict, versioned configuration and small CLI surface: serve, check, and schema honor root precedence, mutation grants, secret references, direct-argv helpers, minimal subprocess environments, cancellation, and redacted logging.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At most one profile loads, its schemaVersion is required, and unknown fields, unsafe paths, duplicate schemes, and invalid grants fail startup.
- [ ] Profile roots and CLI roots cannot be mixed, and all multi-root primary selection follows the accepted authority model.
- [ ] Create, update, and delete grants remain distinct for Workspace Roots and Portable Sources.
- [ ] Secret helpers and configured commands run without a shell, with hard time/output caps and only explicitly allowed environment variables.
- [ ] Protocol stdout remains clean; diagnostics redact secret values and no telemetry is emitted.
- [ ] serve, check, and schema expose their user-visible contracts, and the strict profile schema is fuzzed.

## Blocked by

- rfs-cgbq — Resolve safe multi-root Workspace References

notes.content: rfs-34pz establishes fixed binary/per-call text ceilings, 64 MiB artifact and 256 MiB Path Session ceilings, plus a fixed 24-hour retained-state TTL. This Server Profile issue owns intended future strict fields that may lower output/storage limits and configure the session TTL without raising binary ceilings.

Closed: Implemented the approved Server Profile plan end to end: strict schema/check/probe model, source policies and grants, secret/process/logging controls, immutable serve LaunchPlan, explicit CLI authority, typed exit/channel contract, profile workspace/session/limit application, unsupported-source startup gate, operator documentation, and cross-platform CLI fences. Final evidence: 243 Rust tests plus doctests green with all features and warnings denied; all design claims C1-C33 PASS; 60-second profile fuzz clean; native Windows compiled CLI suite 7/7 green; generated schema hash matches the checked-in fixture.

title: Read configured project Memory Resources
description:
## Parent

## What to build

Expose configured file or directory memory roots through contained read-only memory references with listing, read, search, bounded recovery, and explicit mutation rejection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Configured memory files/directories list, read, and search through canonical memory references.
- [ ] Containment follows canonical targets and rejects traversal or escaping links.
- [ ] Limits, selectors, errors, and Recovery References use the common contracts.
- [ ] Every memory write, edit, delete, or move attempt fails explicitly regardless of workspace grants.
- [ ] The Memory Source Adapter has direct file/directory, missing-content, malformed-content, and containment tests.

## Blocked by

- rfs-vl0u — Search and glob workspace Resources
- rfs-r9m6 — Operate ResourceFS from one strict Server Profile

notes.content: Prioritized per ADR-0005: read-only consolidation win — retires an MCP server from agent configuration. Unblocked once the Server Profile (rfs-r9m6) lands.

Substrate charter: build memory:// as the first instance of a reusable contained-root read substrate extracted from filesystem.rs, not as a one-off adapter. The substrate must carry the existing containment guarantees (cap-std Dir handles, post-open final-path re-resolution, symlink escape rejection, bounded listing/search) parameterized by scheme, configured root(s), and a read-only/mutation policy, while filesystem.rs's workspace-specific authority (WorkspaceRootSet, client root refresh, primary-root relative resolution) stays where it is. Consumers: rfs-cdlp (skill://, rule://), rfs-nb4s (vault:// read side), and rfs-btji (agent://, history://) instantiate the same substrate so symlink-containment code is never duplicated.

title: Search and glob workspace Resources
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Expose bounded discovery through rfs_search and rfs_glob across workspace and artifact Resources, including Rust regex, PCRE2 fallback, ignore and hidden controls, pagination, result limits, and Recovery References.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] rfs_search returns grouped semantic matches for literal, Rust-regex, and PCRE2-only patterns without materializing source content into a prior model turn.
- [ ] Case, ignore, hidden, pagination, skip, and lower-only result-limit controls produce deterministic results.
- [ ] rfs_glob discovers contained files/directories and artifact-backed content without escaping authorized roots.
- [ ] Large result sets remain bounded and preserve omitted results through valid Recovery References.
- [ ] Search and glob cancellation and invalid-pattern failures surface stable observable errors.
- [ ] Filesystem and Artifact Source Adapters are directly exercised through search/glob contract tests.

## Blocked by

- rfs-34pz — Recover bounded reads through Path Session artifacts

notes.content: Implemented bounded Resource discovery across resourcefs-core, Filesystem/Artifact/compiled Source Adapters, and stdio MCP. Delivered Rust-regex-first search with bounded PCRE2 fallback, deterministic controls and diagnostics, contained ignore/hidden traversal, bounded search/glob pagination with immutable Recovery References, root/session fencing, and prompt typed cancellation. Checkpoint commits: 8a8edf2, 3b6313c, 0a76df9, 6098481, a271963, 2a091cd. Final verification: cargo fmt/check; 141 workspace tests across 19 suites; strict all-target/all-feature Clippy; final PCRE2, ignore, and globset probes agree with independent oracles; real resourcefs stdio MCP smoke negotiated 2026-07-28 and exercised read/search/glob successfully. Gilfoyle route and plan record PASS with no FAIL or deferred implementation work.

Closed: Implemented and verified all six acceptance criteria for bounded workspace and Artifact search/glob, including Recovery References, stable errors, direct adapter contracts, full workspace quality gates, independent oracle agreement, and real stdio MCP acceptance.
